classes.name: AccessibilityOptionsRegistry
classes.summary:
Central registry for accessibility option widgets that PolyLib injects into the vanilla Accessibility Options screen.

Mods register providers during client init. PolyLib's event handlers call `#inject(Screen)` on every screen init event. Usage example `// During client init: AccessibilityOptionsRegistry.register("mymod.rescue", target -> { target.addCategory(Component.literal("My Mod")); target.addToggle(Component.literal("Fall Rescue"), prefs::isRescueOn, prefs::setRescueOn); `); }

classes.name: AccessibilityRegistrationBuilder
classes.summary:
Fluent builder for registering accessibility options while simultaneously contributing their default English translations to PolyLib's lang datagen system.

Used with the builder-style `AccessibilityOptionsRegistry#register` overloads: `AccessibilityOptionsRegistry.register("mymod.rescue", builder -> builder .togglePair( "mymod.accessibility.rescue_blink", "Save Me: Blink", () -> prefs.blinkRescueOn, v -> prefs.blinkRescueOn = v, "mymod.accessibility.rescue_farreach", "Save Me: Far Reach", () -> prefs.farReachOn, v -> prefs.farReachOn = v ) .toggle( "mymod.accessibility.void_grave", "Void Grave", () -> prefs.voidGraveOn, v -> prefs.voidGraveOn = v ) ); `

Each method contributes the given key+English pair to `PolyLangContributions` and stores the corresponding widget action. The builder itself implements `OptionsWidgetProvider` and is stored as the entry's provider.

classes.summary:
Central registry for mod config panel screens. Registration tiers

Vanilla Screen — `ScreenFactory)`. Works on any loader. The dev provides a standard `Screen` factory. ModularGui — `GuiProviderFactory)`. PolyLib wraps the `GuiProvider` in a `ModularGuiScreen` automatically. ModularGui Injection — `Predicate, Function)`. Overlays a ModularGui directly onto an existing vanilla screen via `ModularGuiInjector`. Use for advanced cases only.

Auto-hooks

NeoForge — use `NeoForgeConfigHelper.register(...)` from the NeoForge module. This calls both this registry AND `IConfigScreenFactory` so the entry appears under the native "Mods → Config" button. Fabric / Mod Menu — handled automatically via PolyLib's `ModMenuCompat` entrypoint when Mod Menu is present. Just call `#register` from the Fabric init. Button injection fallback — PolyLib injects a button into `ConfigurationSectionScreen` and similar screens that the native hook doesn't cover. Keybinds are also ticked via `#tickKeybinds()`.

PolyConfig json5 backing The per-mod keybind enable/disable map is stored in `polylib.json5` and managed through `PolylibCommon#configData`.

methods.signature: public boolean renderOverlay(GuiRender render, double mouseX, double mouseY, float partialTicks, boolean consumed)
methods.javadoc:
Used to render overlay's such as hover text. Anything rendered in this method will be rendered on top of everything else on the screen. Only one overlay should be rendered at a time, When an element renders content via the overlay method it must return true to indicate the render call has been 'consumed' If the render call has already been consumed (Check via the consumed boolean) then this element should avoid rendering its overlay.

When rendering overlay content, always use the `PoseStack` available via the provided `GuiRender` This stack will already have the correct Z translation to ensure the overlay renders above everything else on the screen.

To check if the cursor is over this element, use 'render.hoveredElement() == this' `#isMouseOver()` Will also work, but may be problematic when multiple, stacked elements have overlay content.

GuiList, as the name suggests allows you to display a list of objects. The list type can be whatever you want, and you can install a converter to map list objects to elements for display.

classes.summary:
This element can be used to create movable/resizable guis of gui elements. This is achieved via a "contentElement" to which all child elements should eb attached. Initially the bounds of the content element will match the parent `GuiManipulable` element. However, depending on which features are enabled, it is possible for the user to resize the content element by clicking and dragging the edges, or move the element by clicking and dragging a specified "dragArea".

It should be noted that the constraints on the underlying `GuiManipulable` should be fairly rigid. Things like dynamic constraint changes will not translate through to the contentElement,

If a UI resize occurs the content element's bounds will be reset to default. You can also trigger a manual reset by calling `#resetBounds()`

classes.name: GuiScrolling
classes.summary:
So the logic behind this element is as follows. This element contains a base "Content Element" that holds all the scrollable content. The content element's position is controlled by the `GuiScrolling` But its `GeoParam#WIDTH` and `GeoParam#HEIGHT` constraints can be set by the user, Or they can be set to dynamically adjust to the child elements added to it.

The bounds of the `GuiScrolling` represent the "view window" When scrolling up/down, left/right the Content Element is effectively just moving around behind the view window and everything outside the view window is scissored off. Any events that occur outside the view window are not propagated to scroll element. Calls to `#isMouseOver()` from an area of an element that is outside the view window will return false.

Elements that are completely outside the view window will not be rendered at all for efficiency.

methods.name: getContentElement
methods.javadoc:
Retrieves the content element that holds all the scrolling elements. You must add all of your scrolling content to this element. Scrolling content must also be constrained relative to this element.

The `GeoParam#TOP` and `GeoParam#LEFT` constraints for this element are set by the `GuiScrolling` and must not be overridden. These are used to control the 'scrolling' of the element.

By default, the `GeoParam#WIDTH` and `GeoParam#HEIGHT` (and therefor also BOTTOM, RIGHT) are dynamically constrained to match the outer bounds of the scrolling elements. So attempting to constrain the content to any of these dynamic parameters would result in a stack overflow. You can however override the WIDTH and HEIGHT constraints if you wish. This can be useful if you wish to create something like a fixed width scrolling list where the width of each scrolling element is bound to the width of the list.

The most important thing to note, Especially when manually constraining the WIDTH and HEIGHT of the content element, All scrolling elements must be withing the bounds of the content element. Anything outside the content element's bounds will not be visible.

methods.name: installContainerElement
methods.javadoc:
This allows you to install a custom container element. The elements constraints will automatically be set by this method.

After calling this method you may override the container element WIDTH and HEIGHT constraints as described in the documentation for `#getContentElement()` But you must not touch the TOP or LEFT constraints.

Important thing to note, By default the container element is preinstalled before any children can be added, meaning any children added to the `GuiScrolling` will render on top of the scrolling content. As this method allows you to set a new child as the container element, any children added before the new content element, will render under the content element.

classes.name: Assembly
classes.summary:
This represents multiple gui elements that have been assembled into a functional component. This is primarily for used by the built-in element builders. But could be used in custom builders.

This is needed because a builder method for an element, cant always return just the relevant element. Take the scroll bar for example. The builtin scroll bar construction consists of a background element, with the scroll bar itself being a child of the background element constrained to the background element.

So the create method for a scroll bar needs to return the background element so that you can constrain int appropriately, but it also needs to return the slider element so that you can actually use it. That's what this container class is for.

classes.name: ElementEvents
classes.summary: This class defines the default implementation for all Screen events. Input events in Modular GUI v2 work similar to v2, events are passed to all elements recursively in a top-down order, and if any element 'consumes' the event, it will not be passed any further down the chain. However, this approach had issues in v2, because there are certain situations where an element needs to receive an event even if it has been consumed. To deal with that we now have two methods for each event, the main handler method that will always get called, and uses a 'consumed' flag to track whether the event has been consumed, as well as a simpler convenience method that will only get called if the event has not already been canceled, and does not require you to call super.

classes.name: ConstrainedGeometry
classes.summary:
This is the base class used to define the size and position of a GuiElement.

The geometry system is designed to be very user-friendly, yet very powerful, with the ability to do all sorts of fun and interesting things. But if all you want is the ability to set simple size and position values, then there is no need to read any further. Just use the basic setters setXPos, setYPos, setWidth, setHeight and everything should just work. If you want to dive deeper, read on.

The geometry system is based around 6 core parameters: xMin, xMax, xSize, yMin, yMax and ySize. See: `GeoParam`

These parameters are defined using 'Constraints' See: `Constraint`

When properly constrained, it will be possible to request values for any of these 6 parameters.

For each axis (x and y) there are 3 constraints: min, max and size.

In order for an axis to be properly defined 2 of these constraints need to be set.

e.g. (xMin and xSize) or (xMin and xMax) or (xMax and xSize)

Using any of these combinations the position and size of an axis can be computed.

Look at `AxisConfig` for details on the values that get returned when too few constraints are set.

TLDR: We will always try to return "reasonable" default values. e.g. if only size is constrained, xMin will default to 0 and xMax will default to 0 + xSize.

If all three constraints are set then the size constraint will be ignored.

You can use `#strictMode(boolean)` to change this behavior.

There are a number of different types of constraints that can be used, including completely custom constraints.

Take a look at the `Constraint` class for a detailed list with explanations.

Note: All position and size values in ModularGui use doubles. This is because floating point position and size values can be very useful at times. But they can also cause a lot of ugly visual artifacts when not used properly. So by default, all the builtin constraints will cast their outputs to an integer value. If you need floating point precision, you can enable it by calling .precise() on any of the builtin constraints.

methods.name: setXPos
methods.javadoc:
Simple method for setting the x position of this element.

Constrains the left side of this element, to the left side of the parent element, with an offset that is calculated by subtracting parent's current x pos from the given x pos.

In other words, if the parent element's position changes, this element will move with it.

methods.name: setYPos
methods.javadoc:
Simple method for setting the y position of this element.

Constrains the top side of this element, to the top side of the parent element, with an offset that is calculated by subtracting parent's current y pos from the given y pos.

In other words, if the parent element's position changes, this element will move with it.

methods.parameters: Material material, Rectangle rectangle, Borders borders, int argb
methods.signature: public void dynamicTex(Material material, Rectangle rectangle, Borders borders, int argb)
methods.javadoc: This can be used to take something like a generic bordered background texture and dynamically resize it to draw at any size and shape you want. This is done by cutting up the texture and stitching it back to together using, cutting and tiling as required. The border parameters indicate the width of the borders around the texture, e.g. a vanilla gui texture has 4 pixel borders.

classes.name: ModularGui
classes.summary: The modular gui system is built around "Gui Elements" but those elements need to be rendered by a base parent element. That's what this class is. This class is essentially just a container for the root gui element.

methods.name: renderScreenBackground
methods.javadoc: Enable / disable the default screen background. (Default Enabled) This will be the usual darkened background when in-game, or the dirt background when not in game.

methods.name: initStandardGui
methods.signature: public ModularGui initStandardGui(int guiWidth, int guiHeight)
methods.javadoc: Sets up this gui to render like any other standards gui with the specified width and height. Meaning, the root element (usually the gui background image) will be centered on the screen, and will have the specified width and height.

methods.name: initFullscreenGui
methods.javadoc: Sets up this gui to render as a full screen gui. Meaning the root element's geometry will match that of the underlying minecraft screen.

methods.name: setVanillaSlotRendering
methods.javadoc:
By default, modular gui completely overrides vanillas default slot rendering. This ensures slots render within the depth constraint of the slot element and avoids situations where stacks in slots render on top of other parts of the gui. Meaning you can do things like hide slots by disabling the slot element, Or render elements on top of the slots.

This method allow you to return full rendering control to vanilla if you need to for whatever reason.

methods.name: render
methods.signature: public void render(GuiRender render, float partialTicks)
methods.javadoc: Primary render method for ModularGui. The screen implementing ModularGui must call this in its render method. Followed by the `float)` method to handle overlay rendering.

methods.name: renderOverlay
methods.signature: public boolean renderOverlay(GuiRender render, float partialTicks)
methods.javadoc:
Handles gui overlay rendering. This is where things like tool tips are rendered. This should be called immediately after `float)`

The reason this is split out from `float)` is to allow stack tool tips to override gui overlay rendering in `ModularGuiContainer`

classes.summary:
NeoForge-specific helper for registering a mod config screen with PolyLib.

A single call to one of these methods registers the screen with both:

`ConfigPanelRegistry` — powers PolyLib's keybind, button injection, and Fabric Mod Menu NeoForge's `IConfigScreenFactory` extension point — makes the screen appear under the native "Mods → Config" button without any extra boilerplate

methods.name: createSlotGroup
methods.signature: protected SlotGroup createSlotGroup(int zoneId, int... quickMoveTo)
methods.javadoc:
Creates and returns a new slot group for this container. You can then add your inventory slots to this slot group, similar to how you would normally add slots to the container. With one big exception! You do not need to worry about setting slot positions! (Just use 0, 0)

Make sure to save your slot groups to accessible fields in your container menu class. You will need to pass these to appropriate `GuiSlots` / `ContainerScreenAccess, SlotGroup, int)` elements. The gui elements will handle positioning and rendering the slots.

As far as splitting a containers slots into multiple groups, Typically the players main inventory and hot bar would be added as two separate groups. How you handle the containers slots is up to you, For something like a machine with several spread out slots, you can still add all the slots to a single group, then pass each individual slot from the group to a single `ContainerScreenAccess, SlotGroup, int)` element. Multiple groups can have the same zone id. Quick move work though the groups in a zone in the order the groups here added.

classes.name: PolyLangContributions
classes.summary:
Central store for PolyLib-managed default English translation strings.

Populated automatically by PolyLib registration APIs:

`AccessibilityRegistrationBuilder` toggle/pair/category methods `ConfigPanelRegistry.register(modId, labelKey, defaultEnglish, ...)` overloads `PlayerClientSettingsRegistry.register(..., displayKey, displayEnglish)` overload `PolyRegistry.register(name, defaultEnglish, supplier)` overload Direct: `String)`

Consumed by `PolyLibLangProvider` in PolyLib's NeoForge module during datagen. Mod lang providers should extend `PolyLibLangProvider` instead of `LanguageProvider` directly to receive all contributions automatically.

Thread-safe. First registration wins — later contributions for an existing key are ignored, allowing mods to override PolyLib defaults by contributing earlier.

This class provides a way to save and synchronize tile data with the client. As well as the ability to set fields in your tile via a client side container screen.

To get started simply define a TileDataManager instance in your tile and call the `#tick()`, and methods from the appropriate methods on your tile.

You can then define a data field in you tile like so: public IntData myIntField = dataManager.register("int_field_name", new IntData(0), SAVE, SYNC, CLIENT_CONTROL);

The SAVE, SYNC and CLIENT_CONTROL flags are each optional, Take a look at #register(String, AbstractDataStore, int...) for more info.

classes.name: PolyLibLangProvider
classes.summary:
Abstract `LanguageProvider` that automatically includes every translation entry contributed to PolyLib's lang datagen system via any PolyLib registration API. Usage Extend this class in your mod's NeoForge datagen module instead of extending `LanguageProvider` directly: `public class ModLangProvider extends PolyLibLangProvider { public ModLangProvider(PackOutput output) { super(output, "mymod"); ` protected void addModTranslations() { // Only entries NOT managed by PolyLib registration APIs. // Items, blocks, and other objects registered with // PolyRegistry.register(name, defaultEnglish, supplier) // and accessibility options registered with // AccessibilityOptionsRegistry.register(key, builder -> ...) // are included AUTOMATICALLY — no add() calls needed here. add("message.mymod.some_event", "Something happened!"); } } } What is auto-included Any key+English pair contributed to `PolyLangContributions` via:

`AccessibilityOptionsRegistry.register(key, builder → ...)` — all `.toggle()`, `.togglePair()`, and `.category()` labels `ConfigPanelRegistry.register(modId, labelKey, defaultEnglish, factory, shortcut)` `ConfigPanelRegistry.registerModularGui(modId, labelKey, defaultEnglish, factory, shortcut)` `PlayerClientSettingsRegistry.register(..., displayNameKey, displayNameEnglish)` `PolyRegistry.register(name, defaultEnglish, supplier)` — block/item names `PolyLangContributions.contribute(key, english)` — direct contributions

Locale support Use `String, String)` to generate a locale other than `en_us`.

methods.name: PolyLibLangProvider
methods.parameters: PackOutput output, String modId, String locale
methods.signature: protected PolyLibLangProvider(PackOutput output, String modId, String locale)

methods.name: addTranslations
methods.javadoc:
Final — do not override. Drains all PolyLib-tracked contributions first, then calls `#addModTranslations()` for mod-specific manual entries.

If a key is contributed by both PolyLib and `addModTranslations()`, the manual call in `addModTranslations()` will overwrite the PolyLib default, giving mods full control to customise any auto-contributed string.

methods.name: addModTranslations
methods.javadoc:
Override to add translation entries NOT automatically contributed via PolyLib APIs.

You do NOT need to add entries for:

Items/blocks registered via `PolyRegistry.register(name, english, supplier)` Accessibility toggle labels registered via `AccessibilityOptionsRegistry.register(key, builder)` Config panel button labels registered via the string-key overloads of `ConfigPanelRegistry` Settings type display names registered via the display-name overloads of `PlayerClientSettingsRegistry`

You DO still need to add entries for:

Items/blocks registered with the old `register(name, supplier)` overload (no English provided) Chat messages, tooltips, subtitles, and any other keys not tied to a PolyLib registration

classes.name: NeoForgeDebugBridge
classes.summary:
NeoForge bridge that wires `PolyDebugRegistry` into the vanilla `DebugScreenEntries` system via `RegisterDebugEntriesEvent`.

Registered on the mod event bus from `net.creeperhost.polylib.PolyLibClientNeoForge`.

Each `PolyDebugEntryType` is adapted to a `DebugScreenEntry` that delegates `isAllowed()` and `display()` back to the `PolyDebugEntry` implementation. Toggle state and persistence are handled entirely by vanilla's `DebugOptions` / `options.txt` mechanism — no extra storage is needed.

classes.name: PolyDebugDisplayer
classes.summary:
Platform-agnostic display interface passed to `PolyDebugEntry#display`.

Maps directly onto `DebugScreenDisplayer` on both NeoForge and Fabric. Use `#addLine` for normal sequential lines, `#addPriorityLine` to force a line to the top of its column, and `#addToGroup` to append lines beneath an existing vanilla or mod-registered entry group.

classes.name: PolyDebugEntry
classes.summary:
Callback interface for a custom F3 debug screen entry.

Implement this interface and register an instance via `PolyDebugRegistry#register`. Both methods are called on the render thread (client-side only), each frame while the F3 screen is visible. Example `PolyDebugRegistry.register( Identifier.fromNamespaceAndPath("mymod", "stats"), new PolyDebugEntry() { public boolean isAllowed(Minecraft mc, boolean reduced) { return mc.level != null; // only show in-world ` public void display(PolyDebugDisplayer d, Level level, LevelChunk cc, LevelChunk sc) { d.addLine("MyMod stat: " + MyStats.getValue()); } }, true, true, false, "debug.mymod.stats", "My Stats" ); }

classes.name: PolyDebugEntryType
classes.summary:
Typed registration token for a custom F3 debug screen entry.

Obtain via `PolyDebugRegistry#register` and store as a `public static final` constant in your mod class. Toggle / profile behaviour

`#defaultEnabled` — whether the toggle button is ON by default when no saved preference exists yet. MC persists the toggle across sessions in the vanilla `options.txt` (`debugScreen.*`). `#inDefaultProfile` — automatically enable this entry when the player activates the "Default" F3 profile (F3 + N in vanilla). `#inPerformanceProfile` — automatically enable this entry when the "Performance" F3 profile is active.

methods.name: id
methods.javadoc: Namespaced registration ID, e.g. `"mymod:my_entry"`.

methods.name: entry
methods.javadoc: The entry callback implementation.

methods.name: defaultEnabled
methods.javadoc: Whether the F3 toggle for this entry starts in the ON position when no saved state exists. Vanilla persists the toggle in `options.txt`.

methods.name: inDefaultProfile
methods.javadoc: Whether this entry is included in the "Default" F3 debug profile.

methods.name: inPerformanceProfile
methods.javadoc: Whether this entry is included in the "Performance" F3 debug profile.

methods.name: displayNameKey
methods.javadoc: Optional translation key for the toggle label shown in the F3 options menu. May be `null` if no name was registered, in which case the raw `#id()` string will typically be used as the label.

classes.name: PolyDebugRegistry
classes.summary:
Registry for `PolyDebugEntryType` tokens.

Registration must happen before the debug screen is first opened — typically in your mod's client initialiser or static init. On NeoForge this registry is consumed by `net.creeperhost.polylib.debug.neoforge.NeoForgeDebugBridge` during the `RegisterDebugEntriesEvent` (mod bus). On Fabric it is consumed by the `FabricDebugEntriesMixin` injected into `DebugScreenEntries`. Minimal usage example `// In your mod client init: public static final PolyDebugEntryType MY_ENTRY = PolyDebugRegistry.register( Identifier.fromNamespaceAndPath("mymod", "my_info"), displayer -> displayer.addLine("MyMod: " + getSomeValue()), true, // ON by default true, // included in the Default profile false, // not in the Performance profile "debug.mymod.my_info", // i18n key "My Info" // English fallback for datagen ); `

Fired to allow modification of fog density and extent. Mutate `params[0]` (near plane) and `params[1]` (far plane).

NeoForge: `ViewportEvent.RenderFog`

Fabric: no equivalent (NeoForge-primary)

fields.name: COMPUTE_FOV
fields.javadoc:
Fired to allow modification of the computed (absolute) field-of-view angle. Mutate `fov[0]` to override the FOV (in degrees).

This is the absolute FOV, distinct from the FOV modifier/multiplier in `PolyCameraEvents#FOV_MODIFIER`.

NeoForge: `ViewportEvent.ComputeFov`

Fabric: no equivalent (NeoForge-primary)

fields.name: COMPUTE_CAMERA_DISTANCE
fields.javadoc:
Fired to allow modification of the third-person (detached) camera distance. Mutate `distance[0]` to override the distance.

NeoForge: `CalculateDetachedCameraDistanceEvent`

Fabric: no equivalent (NeoForge-primary)

classes.name: PolyBlockEntityEvents
classes.summary: Events related to block entity lifecycle (load / unload).

fields.name: BLOCK_ENTITY_LOAD
fields.javadoc:
Fired when a block entity is loaded into the world (chunk load or placement).

NeoForge: mixin on `Level#addBlockEntity`

Fabric: mixin on `Level#addBlockEntity`

fields.name: BLOCK_ENTITY_UNLOAD
fields.javadoc:
Fired when a block entity is unloaded from the world (chunk unload or removal).

NeoForge: mixin on `Level#removeBlockEntity`

Fabric: mixin on `Level#removeBlockEntity`

fields.name: BREAK
fields.javadoc:
Fired before a player breaks a block. Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to prevent the break.

NeoForge: `BreakBlockEvent` (cancellable)

Fabric: `PlayerBlockBreakEvents.BEFORE` (boolean gate)

fields.name: PLACE
fields.javadoc:
Fired when any entity places a block. Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to prevent the placement.

NeoForge: `BlockEvent.EntityPlaceEvent` (cancellable)

Fabric: no native equivalent — NeoForge-only cancel support

fields.name: CROP_GROW_PRE
fields.javadoc:
Fired before a crop grows (natural or bonemeal). Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to prevent growth.

NeoForge: `CropGrowEvent.Pre` (result-based cancel)

Fabric: mixin into `CropBlock#grow`

fields.name: CROP_GROW_POST
fields.javadoc:
Fired after a crop has grown.

NeoForge: `CropGrowEvent.Post`

Fabric: mixin into `CropBlock#grow` RETURN

fields.name: FARMLAND_TRAMPLE
fields.javadoc:
Fired when an entity tramples farmland. Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to prevent trampling.

NeoForge: `BlockEvent.FarmlandTrampleEvent` (cancellable)

Fabric: no native equivalent — NeoForge-only cancel support

fields.name: PORTAL_SPAWN
fields.javadoc:
Fired when a Nether portal frame is about to generate portal blocks. Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to prevent the portal from spawning.

NeoForge: `BlockEvent.PortalSpawnEvent`

Fabric: mixin into `PortalShape#createPortalBlocks`

fields.name: PISTON_PRE
fields.javadoc:
Fired before a piston extends or retracts. Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to prevent the piston from moving.

NeoForge: `PistonEvent.Pre`

Fabric: mixin into `PistonBaseBlock#triggerEvent`

fields.name: PISTON_POST
fields.javadoc:
Fired after a piston has extended or retracted. Not cancellable.

NeoForge: `PistonEvent.Post`

Fabric: mixin into `PistonBaseBlock#triggerEvent` at RETURN

fields.name: NOTE_BLOCK_PLAY
fields.javadoc:
Fired when a note block is about to play its note. Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to silence the note.

NeoForge: `NoteBlockEvent.Play`

Fabric: mixin into `NoteBlock#triggerEvent`

fields.name: FLUID_SOURCE
fields.javadoc:
Fired when a flowing fluid is about to convert into a source block. Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to prevent the conversion.

NeoForge: `CreateFluidSourceEvent` (uses `setCanConvert(false)`)

Fabric: mixin into `FlowingFluid#spreadTo`

fields.name: BLOCK_DROPS
fields.javadoc:
Fired when a broken block is computing its drops. Modify the `drops` list to change results.

NeoForge: `BlockDropsEvent`

Fabric: mixin on `Block#dropResources`

fields.name: ENTITY_MULTI_PLACE
fields.javadoc:
Fired when an entity places multiple blocks at once (door, bed, etc.). Cancellable.

NeoForge: `BlockEvent.EntityMultiPlaceEvent`

Fabric: no native equivalent

fields.name: FLUID_PLACE_BLOCK
fields.javadoc:
Fired when a flowing fluid places a solid block (obsidian, cobblestone, etc.). Cancellable.

NeoForge: `BlockEvent.FluidPlaceBlockEvent`

Fabric: mixin on `FlowingFluid#spreadTo`

fields.name: NEIGHBOR_NOTIFY
fields.javadoc:
Fired when a block notifies its neighbors of a state change. Not cancellable.

NeoForge: `BlockEvent.NeighborNotifyEvent`

Fabric: mixin on `Level#updateNeighborsAt`

fields.name: BLOCK_GROW_FEATURE
fields.javadoc:
Fired when a block feature (mushroom, tree, azalea, etc.) grows in the world. Not cancellable.

NeoForge: `BlockGrowFeature`

Fabric: mixin on `BonemealableBlock#performBonemeal`

fields.name: ALTER_GROUND
fields.javadoc:
Fired when ground blocks are altered by tree/feature generation. Not cancellable.

NeoForge: `AlterGroundEvent`

Fabric: mixin on `AlterGroundDecorator#place`

fields.name: NOTE_BLOCK_CHANGE
fields.javadoc:
Fired when a note block's note is changed by a player right-click. Cancellable.

NeoForge: `NoteBlockEvent.Change`

Fabric: mixin on `NoteBlock#use`

classes.name: PolyBrewingEvents
classes.summary:
Events related to brewing stand operations.

NeoForge: `PotionBrewEvent.Pre` / `PotionBrewEvent.Post`

Fabric: mixin into `BrewingStandBlockEntity#doTick`

fields.name: BREW_PRE
fields.javadoc:
Fired before a brewing operation completes. Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to prevent the brew from being applied.

`items` is the live item list of the brewing stand (slots 0-2 are outputs, slot 3 is the ingredient, slot 4 is the fuel). Handlers may modify the list in place to alter the brew result.

NeoForge: `PotionBrewEvent.Pre` (cancellable)

Fabric: mixin into `BrewingStandBlockEntity#doTick` at INVOKE of the actual brew

fields.name: BREW_POST
fields.javadoc:
Fired after a brewing operation has completed successfully. Observer only — not cancellable.

NeoForge: `PotionBrewEvent.Post`

Fabric: mixin into `BrewingStandBlockEntity#doTick` at INVOKE (post)

classes.name: PolyChatEvents
classes.summary: Events related to player chat messages and command execution.

fields.name: SERVER_CHAT
fields.javadoc:
Fired when a player sends a chat message to the server. Cancel to suppress the message; modify `message[0]` to change content.

NeoForge: `ServerChatEvent`

Fabric: mixin on `PlayerList#broadcastChatMessage`

fields.name: COMMAND_EXECUTE
fields.javadoc:
Fired when a command is being executed (player or command block). Cancel to prevent execution; modify `command[0]` to change command text.

NeoForge: `CommandEvent`

Fabric: mixin on `Commands#performPrefixedCommand`

fields.name: ALLOW_GAME_MESSAGE
fields.javadoc:
Gate event: return `false` from any handler to suppress a system/game message from being broadcast.

NeoForge: mixin on `MinecraftServer#sendSystemMessage` at HEAD

Fabric: `ServerMessageEvents.ALLOW_GAME_MESSAGE`

fields.name: SERVER_GAME_MESSAGE
fields.javadoc:
Observer fired when the server broadcasts a game/system message to all players.

NeoForge: mixin on `MinecraftServer#sendSystemMessage` at RETURN

Fabric: `ServerMessageEvents.GAME_MESSAGE`

fields.name: CHAT_DECORATE
fields.javadoc:
Decoration hook: modify the outgoing chat `Component` before it is sent. `message[0]` starts as the player's original component; each handler may replace it by writing a new value into the array.

NeoForge: `ServerChatEvent` (mutate the component before the normal chat dispatch path)

Fabric: `ServerMessageDecoratorEvent.EVENT`

fields.name: CHUNK_WATCH
fields.javadoc:
Fired when a player starts watching (tracking) a chunk.

NeoForge: `ChunkWatchEvent.Watch`

Fabric: mixin on `ChunkMap#updateChunkTracking` or `PlayerChunkSender`

fields.name: CHUNK_UNWATCH
fields.javadoc:
Fired when a player stops watching (tracking) a chunk.

NeoForge: `ChunkWatchEvent.UnWatch`

Fabric: mixin on chunk tracking logic

classes.name: PolyDataEvents
classes.summary:
Events related to data/resource loading.

Note: `REGISTER_COMMANDS` is located in `PolyServerCommandEvents`.

fields.name: TAGS_UPDATED
fields.javadoc:
Fired after tags are loaded or reloaded on the server (startup and `/reload`).

NeoForge: `TagsUpdatedEvent` (SERVER_DATA_LOAD cause only)

Fabric: no direct equivalent — NeoForge only initially (TODO: Fabric bridge)

fields.name: LOOT_TABLE_LOAD
fields.javadoc:
Fired when a loot table is being loaded from data packs.

NeoForge: `LootTableLoadEvent` (game bus)

Fabric: mixin on `LootDataManager` loading path

classes.name: PolyEnchantEvents
classes.summary: Events related to enchanting mechanics.

fields.name: GET_ENCHANT_LEVEL
fields.javadoc:
Fired to adjust the effective enchantment level of an item. Modify `enchantments` (it is a `ItemEnchantments.Mutable`) to change results.

NeoForge: `GetEnchantmentLevelEvent` (GAME bus)

Fabric: mixin on `EnchantmentHelper#getEnchantmentLevel`

fields.name: ENCHANT_TABLE_LEVEL
fields.javadoc:
Fired to adjust the level offered in an enchanting table slot. Modify `level[0]`.

NeoForge: `EnchantmentLevelSetEvent` (GAME bus)

Fabric: mixin on `EnchantingTableBlockEntity#tick`

fields.name: ENTITY_TICK
fields.javadoc: Fired every tick for each entity that is ticking (server-side). Equivalent to NeoForge `EntityTickEvent.Post`.

fields.name: ENTITY_TICK_END
fields.javadoc:
Fired after an entity's tick method completes. Completes the entity tick pair.

NeoForge: `EntityTickEvent.Post`

Fabric: mixin on `Entity#tick` at RETURN

fields.name: JOIN_LEVEL
fields.javadoc:
Fired when an entity is about to join a server level. Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to prevent the entity from joining. Equivalent to NeoForge `EntityJoinLevelEvent`.

Note: cancellation is not supported on Fabric via the direct lifecycle event.

fields.name: MOUNT
fields.javadoc:
Fired when an entity is about to mount or dismount a vehicle. Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to prevent the mount/dismount.

NeoForge: `EntityMountEvent` (cancellable)

Fabric: mixin into `Entity#startRiding`

fields.name: LEAVE_LEVEL
fields.javadoc:
Fired when an entity leaves a server level (is unloaded or removed). Informational — not cancellable.

NeoForge: `EntityLeaveLevelEvent`

Fabric: `ServerEntityEvents.ENTITY_UNLOAD`

fields.name: TELEPORT
fields.javadoc:
Fired when an entity is about to teleport (within the same level). Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to prevent the teleport.

NeoForge: `EntityTeleportEvent`

Fabric: mixin into `Entity#teleportTo`

fields.name: TRAVEL_DIMENSION
fields.javadoc:
Fired when an entity is about to travel to a different dimension. Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to prevent the dimension change.

Note: cancellation is not supported on Fabric (fires post-change via `ServerEntityLevelChangeEvents.AFTER_ENTITY_CHANGE_WORLD`).

NeoForge: `EntityTravelToDimensionEvent` (cancellable)

fields.name: MOB_GRIEFING
fields.javadoc:
Fired when the game checks whether a mob is allowed to grief (break blocks, etc.). Set the result via `GriefingContext#setCanGrief(boolean)`.

NeoForge: `EntityMobGriefingEvent`

Fabric: no direct equivalent (TODO: mixin)

fields.name: PROJECTILE_IMPACT
fields.javadoc:
Fired when a projectile impacts a block or entity. Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to prevent processing the impact.

NeoForge: `ProjectileImpactEvent`

Fabric: mixin into `Projectile#hitTargetOrDeflectSelf`

fields.name: STRUCK_BY_LIGHTNING
fields.javadoc:
Fired when an entity is about to be struck by a lightning bolt. Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to prevent the strike.

NeoForge: `EntityStruckByLightningEvent`

Fabric: mixin into `Entity#thunderHit`

fields.name: ENTITY_INVULNERABILITY_CHECK
fields.javadoc:
Fires when the engine checks whether an entity is invulnerable to a damage source. Each handler receives the accumulated result from prior handlers and may flip it.

NeoForge: `EntityInvulnerabilityCheckEvent`

Fabric: mixin on `Entity#isInvulnerableTo` at RETURN

fields.name: ENTITY_CHANGE_LEVEL_POST
fields.javadoc:
Observer fired after a non-player entity has fully completed a dimension change. `original` is the entity that entered the portal; `replacement` is the new instance in the destination level. Player dimension changes are covered by `PolyPlayerEvents.CHANGE_DIMENSION`.

NeoForge: mixin on `Entity#changeDimension` at RETURN

Fabric: `ServerEntityLevelChangeEvents.AFTER_ENTITY_CHANGE_LEVEL`

fields.name: START
fields.javadoc:
Fired when an explosion starts, before any blocks or entities are affected. Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to prevent the explosion.

NeoForge: `ExplosionEvent.Start` (cancellable)

Fabric: no native equivalent — NeoForge-only cancel support

fields.name: DETONATE
fields.javadoc:
Fired after the explosion has calculated the list of affected blocks and entities. Handlers may read (or via NeoForge modify) the affected lists.

NeoForge: `ExplosionEvent.Detonate`

Fabric: no native equivalent

fields.name: KNOCKBACK
fields.javadoc:
Fired when explosion knockback velocity is being applied to an entity.

NeoForge: `ExplosionKnockbackEvent`

Fabric: no native equivalent

methods.name: AnvilContext
methods.parameters: ItemStack output, int xpCost, int materialCost
methods.signature: public AnvilContext(ItemStack output, int xpCost, int materialCost)

fields.name: ITEM_USE_START
fields.javadoc:
Fired when a living entity starts using an item (bow draw, eating, etc.). Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to prevent use from starting. Includes `duration` — the total use-ticks of this item.

NeoForge: `LivingEntityUseItemEvent.Start`

Fabric: mixin into `LivingEntity#startUsingItem`

fields.name: ITEM_USE_TICK
fields.javadoc:
Fired each tick while a living entity is using an item. Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to stop the use mid-tick. `ticksRemaining` counts down from the total duration.

NeoForge: `LivingEntityUseItemEvent.Tick`

Fabric: mixin into `LivingEntity#updatingUsingItem` tick path

fields.name: ITEM_USE_FINISH
fields.javadoc:
Fired when a living entity finishes using an item (use completed fully). Informational only — cannot be cancelled at this stage.

NeoForge: `LivingEntityUseItemEvent.Finish`

Fabric: mixin into `LivingEntity#completeUsingItem`

fields.name: ITEM_EXPIRE
fields.javadoc:
Fired when an `ItemEntity` expires naturally (lifespan runs out). Informational only — cannot be cancelled.

NeoForge: `ItemExpireEvent`

Fabric: mixin into `ItemEntity#tick`

fields.name: ITEM_FISHING
fields.javadoc:
Fired when a fishing hook retrieves its catch. Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to prevent the items being spawned.

NeoForge: `ItemFishedEvent` (cancellable)

Fabric: mixin into `FishingHook#retrieve`

fields.name: GRINDSTONE
fields.javadoc:
Fired when items are placed in a grindstone and the output is computed. Use `GrindstoneContext` to read or modify the output and XP.

NeoForge: `GrindstoneEvent.OnPlaceItem`

Fabric: mixin into `GrindstoneMenu#slotsChanged`

fields.name: ANVIL_UPDATE
fields.javadoc:
Fired when the anvil computes a repair or rename result. Use `AnvilContext` to read or modify the output, XP cost, and material cost.

NeoForge: `AnvilUpdateEvent`

Fabric: mixin into `AnvilMenu#createResult`

fields.name: FUEL_BURN_TIME
fields.javadoc:
Fired to query how long an item burns as fuel. Modify `burnTime[0]` to change.

NeoForge: `FurnaceFuelBurnTimeEvent` (MOD bus)

Fabric: mixin on `FurnaceBlockEntity#getBurnDuration`

fields.name: ITEM_STACKED_ON_OTHER
fields.javadoc:
Fired when a player drags/stacks one inventory item onto another. Informational only.

NeoForge: `ItemStackedOnOtherEvent`

Fabric: mixin on `AbstractContainerMenu#doClick` stack-merge branch

fields.name: ANVIL_CRAFT
fields.javadoc:
Fired after an item is successfully crafted/renamed in an anvil. Informational only.

NeoForge: `AnvilCraftEvent.Post`

Fabric: mixin on the result slot's `onTake` callback in `AnvilMenu`

fields.name: SLEEP_FINISHED
fields.javadoc:
Fired when players finish sleeping and the day advances. Informational only.

NeoForge: `SleepFinishedTimeEvent`

Fabric: mixin into `ServerLevel#updateSleepingPlayerList`

fields.name: GAME_RULE_CHANGE
fields.javadoc:
Fired when a game rule value changes. Informational.

NeoForge: `GameRuleChangedEvent` (MOD bus)

Fabric: mixin on `GameRule#set`

fields.name: DIFFICULTY_CHANGE
fields.javadoc:
Fired when the world difficulty changes. Informational.

NeoForge: `DifficultyChangeEvent` (GAME bus)

Fabric: mixin on `MinecraftServer#setDifficulty`

fields.name: POTENTIAL_SPAWNS
fields.javadoc:
Fired when gathering potential spawn entries for a chunk. Modify the list to add/remove spawns.

NeoForge: `LevelEvent.PotentialSpawns`

Fabric: mixin on `NaturalSpawner#getFilteredSpawnableEntities`

methods.signature: public BreatheContext(boolean canBreathe, int consumeAirAmount, int refillAirAmount)

fields.name: DAMAGE_PRE
fields.javadoc: Fired before incoming damage is applied (before armor/enchantment calc). Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to prevent the damage.

fields.name: DAMAGE_POST
fields.javadoc: Fired after damage has been applied.

fields.name: DEATH
fields.javadoc: Fired when a living entity is about to die. Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to prevent the death.

fields.name: FALL
fields.javadoc: Fired when a living entity lands from a fall. distance is in blocks (double).

fields.name: DROPS
fields.javadoc: Fired when a living entity generates drops on death.

fields.name: XP_DROP
fields.javadoc: Fired when a living entity is about to drop XP on death.

fields.name: DAMAGE_FINAL_PRE
fields.javadoc: Fired before damage is applied but after armor/enchantment reduction (post-armor, pre-application). This matches NeoForge `LivingDamageEvent.Pre`. Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to prevent the damage.

fields.name: HEAL
fields.javadoc: Fired when a living entity is being healed. Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to prevent the healing.

fields.name: CHANGE_TARGET
fields.javadoc: Fired when a mob is changing its attack target. Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to prevent the target change.

fields.name: CONVERSION_PRE
fields.javadoc:
Fired before a living entity converts to another type (e.g. zombie to drowned). Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to prevent the conversion.

Note: Fabric cancel not supported without a mixin.

fields.name: CONVERSION_POST
fields.javadoc:
Fired after a living entity has converted to another type.

Fabric: bridged via `ServerLivingEntityEvents.MOB_CONVERSION`.

fields.name: KNOCKBACK
fields.javadoc: Fired when a living entity is being knocked back. Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to prevent the knockback.

fields.name: USE_TOTEM
fields.javadoc:
Fired when a living entity is about to use a Totem of Undying. Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to prevent the totem from triggering.

Note: Fabric cancel support is best-effort (see mixin).

fields.name: CRITICAL_HIT
fields.javadoc:
Fired when a player performs a melee attack to determine if it is a critical hit. Use `CriticalHitContext` to override whether the hit is critical and the damage multiplier.

NeoForge: `CriticalHitEvent`

Fabric: TODO (non-trivial local capture in `Player#attack`)

fields.name: ARROW_NOCK
fields.javadoc:
Fired when a player begins drawing a bow. Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to prevent drawing.

NeoForge: `ArrowNockEvent`

Fabric: mixin into `BowItem#use`

fields.name: ARROW_LOOSE
fields.javadoc:
Fired when a player releases a drawn bow (fires the arrow). Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to prevent firing.

NeoForge: `ArrowLooseEvent`

Fabric: mixin into `BowItem#releaseUsing`

fields.name: SHIELD_BLOCK

Fired when a living entity attempts to block damage with a shield. Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to bypass the block (shield doesn't absorb).

fields.name: ENTITY_EQUIP_CHANGE
fields.javadoc:
Fired when a living entity changes an equipment slot (armour, hand, etc.). Informational only.

NeoForge: `LivingEquipmentChangeEvent`

Fabric: mixin into `LivingEntity#onEquipItem`

fields.name: ITEM_USE_START
fields.javadoc:
Fired when a living entity starts using an item (e.g. eating, drawing bow). Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to prevent the use from starting.

NeoForge: `LivingEntityUseItemEvent.Start`

Fabric: mixin into `LivingEntity#startUsingItem`

fields.name: ITEM_USE_FINISH
fields.javadoc:
Fired when a living entity finishes using an item. Modify `resultHolder[0]` to override the resulting stack.

NeoForge: `LivingEntityUseItemEvent.Finish`

Fabric: mixin into `LivingEntity#completeUsingItem`

fields.name: MOB_SPLIT
fields.javadoc:
Fired when a slime-like mob is about to split into smaller copies. Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to prevent the split.

NeoForge: `MobSplitEvent`

Fabric: mixin into `Slime#remove`

fields.name: BABY_SPAWN
fields.javadoc:
Fired when two animals are about to produce a baby. Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to prevent the baby from spawning.

NeoForge: `BabyEntitySpawnEvent`

Fabric: mixin into `Animal#spawnChildFromBreeding`

fields.name: DROWN

NeoForge: `LivingDrownEvent`

Fabric: mixin stub (best-effort)

fields.name: BREATHE

NeoForge: `LivingBreatheEvent`

Fabric: mixin stub (best-effort)

fields.name: DESTROY_BLOCK
fields.javadoc:
Fired when a living entity destroys a block (e.g. Enderman picking up a block). Call `CancelContext#cancel()` to prevent the block from being destroyed.

NeoForge: `LivingDestroyBlockEvent`

fields.name: GET_PROJECTILE

Fired when a living entity is determining which projectile to use. Modify `resultHolder[0]` to override the chosen projectile stack.

NeoForge: `LivingGetProjectileEvent`

Fabric: mixin into `LivingEntity#getProjectile`

fields.name: SWAP_ITEMS

fields.name: SPAWN_CLUSTER_SIZE
fields.javadoc:
Fired when determining the cluster size for a mob spawn. Modify `size` field to change.

NeoForge: `SpawnClusterSizeEvent`

Fabric: mixin on `Mob#getMaxSpawnClusterSize`

fields.name: ENDERMAN_ANGER
fields.javadoc:
Fired when an Enderman begins to get angry at a player. Cancel to prevent.

NeoForge: `EnderManAngerEvent`

Fabric: mixin on `EnderMan#isLookingAtMe`

fields.name: ENTITY_KILLED_OTHER
fields.javadoc:
Fired when a living entity kills another living entity. Informational.

fields.name: ARMOR_HURT

Fabric: mixin on `LivingEntity#hurtArmor`

fields.name: ELYTRA_ALLOW

classes.summary:
Events related to registry operations.

Tier 15 — `REGISTRY_ID_REMAP` added in Tier 15.

fields.name: REGISTRY_ID_REMAP
fields.javadoc:
Fires when registry integer IDs are remapped during world load (e.g. when mods are added/removed and the block/item ID table needs updating).

Fabric-primary; NeoForge handles ID remapping internally with no accessible event hook. `remapState` is a Fabric `RegistryIdRemapCallback.RemapState` on Fabric; on NeoForge this event is never fired (no-op).

Fabric: `RegistryIdRemapCallback.event(registry)`

fields.name: MODIFY_DIMENSION_ATTRIBUTES
fields.javadoc:
Fires when a dimension's world generation attributes are being modified. Handlers receive loader-specific objects as `Object` references to avoid coupling common code to Fabric API.

Fabric-only: `DimensionEvents.MODIFY_ATTRIBUTES`

NeoForge: no equivalent (event never fires — no-op).

On Fabric the three arguments are, in order:

`Holder` — the dimension type holder `EnvironmentAttributeMap.Builder` — the attribute builder to modify `HolderLookup.Provider` — the registry lookup provider

On NeoForge all three are always `null`.

classes.name: EntryMapAccessor
classes.summary:
Mixin accessor that exposes the private-static `ENTRIES_BY_ID` field of `DebugScreenEntries` so that `FabricDebugEntriesMixin` can insert PolyLib debug entries after vanilla's static initialiser runs.

Mutable access is intentional: we need to `Map#put` into the live map, not a copy. The field is a `HashMap` (confirmed via bytecode) that is later read (but not replaced) by `allEntries()` and `getEntry()`.

classes.name: FabricDebugEntriesMixin
classes.summary:
Fabric bridge for `PolyDebugRegistry`.

Injects at the tail of `DebugScreenEntries`'s static initialiser so that all entries registered via `PolyDebugRegistry` are appended to the vanilla `ENTRIES_BY_ID` map before the first F3 screen render.

Because `register(Identifier, DebugScreenEntry)` is private-static, we obtain the `ENTRIES_BY_ID` field via the `EntryMapAccessor` interface and call `Map#put` directly. This matches exactly what the private method does (see bytecode: `ENTRIES_BY_ID.put(id, entry); return id;`).

classes.name: OfflinePlayerData
classes.summary:
Mutable view of a single player's PolyLib server data, valid for either an online or offline player. Obtained via `java.util.UUID, java.util.function.Consumer)`.

For online players every `#get`/`#set` call goes directly to `net.creeperhost.polylib.player.serverdata.PlayerServerDataManager`. For offline players the view is backed by the loaded `ForgeData` `net.minecraft.nbt.CompoundTag`; changes are written back to `/playerdata/.dat` when the `modify` call returns.

classes.name: OfflinePlayerDataAccessor
classes.summary: Read/write PolyLib `PlayerServerDataType` values for both online and offline players. Online players All operations delegate to the live `PlayerServerDataManager` so the in-memory store is never bypassed. Offline players Data is read from / written to the player's `.dat` file at `/playerdata/.dat`. The exact NBT structure used is platform-specific: NeoForge stores data inside the `ForgeData` compound; Fabric uses the `fabric:attachments` compound. Thread safety Must be called from the server tick thread. No locking is performed because Minecraft's server is single-threaded; concurrent calls from other threads (e.g. the network thread) are unsafe regardless. Usage example `// One-shot read (returns default if no data) PlayerAbilities ab = OfflinePlayerDataAccessor.get(server, uuid, ModPlayerData.PLAYER_ABILITIES); // One-shot write OfflinePlayerDataAccessor.set(server, uuid, ModPlayerData.PLAYER_ABILITIES, newAbilities); // Atomic read-modify-write (single file I/O pass for offline players) OfflinePlayerDataAccessor.modify(server, uuid, data -> { PlayerAbilities ab = data.get(ModPlayerData.PLAYER_ABILITIES); ab.addPower(SomePower.ID); data.set(ModPlayerData.PLAYER_ABILITIES, ab); `); }

classes.summary:
Client-side read-only cache of server-authoritative player data values.

Values are received via `SyncPlayerServerDataS2CPayload` and decoded on demand using the type's `syncCodec`. This cache is keyed by type ID only (not UUID) because these values are always for the local/owning player.

Typical use: HUD rendering, client-side power availability checks. Never write to this; mutations go through `PlayerServerDataManager#set` on the server.

classes.name: PlayerServerDataManager
classes.summary:
Central server-side manager for `PlayerServerDataType` values.

Handles NBT persistence (via `IPlayerDataHelper`), optional S2C sync to the owning player, and player lifecycle (login / logout / respawn).

Server is always the authoritative source. Use `#get` / `#set` from server-side code only. Clients receive a read-only copy via `PlayerServerDataClientCache` when the type's `syncCodec` is non-null.

methods.javadoc:
Returns the current value for a player. Server-side only. Returns the type's default if the player has no active store.

Lazy-load: if the store exists but has never seen this type (i.e. the type was registered after `PlayerLoggedInEvent` fired due to Java's lazy class initialisation), we attempt a single NBT read from the player's persistent data before returning the default. This makes registration order irrelevant in production and removes the need for mods to call a no-op `init()` method to force-load their registry class.

Registers a new object and contributes its default English translation to PolyLib's lang datagen system.

The translation key is derived automatically using Minecraft's standard pattern: `".."`, e.g. `"item.mymod.void_blade"`. This matches the default key returned by `Item.getDescriptionId()` and `Block.getDescriptionId()`.

Mod lang providers extending `PolyLibLangProvider` receive this entry automatically — no manual `add()` call needed.

methods.javadoc:
Registers a `CreativeModeTab`, automatically contributing the default English title translation using the standard `itemGroup..` key.

On NeoForge this delegates to the underlying `net.neoforged.neoforge.registries.DeferredRegister` and is flushed when `NeoPolyRegistry.registerToBus(bus)` is called in the mod constructor. On Fabric, `#init()` must be called from `ModInitializer.onInitialize()`.

Usage: `public static final PolyRegistry TABS = PolyRegistry.create(Registries.CREATIVE_MODE_TAB, MY_MOD_ID); public static final Supplier MY_TAB = TABS.registerCreativeTab( "my_tab", "My Mod", () -> new ItemStack(Items.DIAMOND), (params, output) -> output.accept(MyItems.MY_ITEM.get()) ); ` `output.accept(item)` to populate the tab
